newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a day of cross-fire for Australian soccer, departing Socceroos coach Eddie Thomson fired at Soccer Australia commissioner George Negus, claiming Negus had been trying to undermine him for months. Meanwhile former Socceroos coach Frank Arok lashed out at Thomson, saying the game had not gone forward under him. Page 20.

Prominent national Socceroos and Soccer Australia chairman, David Hill, is set to clash over players' demands for the payment of prize money. The Socceroos are prepared to boycott the return leg of the Oceania Nations Cup if their demands for an improved financial package are not met. Page 20.

Olympic gold-medal-winning hockey coach Ric Charlesworth has chosen to remain with the national women's hockey team, leaving the door open for former team-mate Terry Walsh to take the coaching position for the national men's team. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's richest sportsman, Greg Norman, has revealed he would seek advice from Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer. Norman claims the best advice Packer gave was not about how to play the golfing game, but business advice which will lead to Norman gossing US$60 million this year. Page 44.

After believing the worst had passed, the Australian Rugby League was stunned last night by the possibility that Optus Vision may not have the required funds for the A$120 million ARL rescue package. A key Optus Vision shareholder, The Seven Network, claimed the pay-TV giant may not have the capacity to prop-up the ARL whilst current legal action was underway. Page 44.

The Gai Waterhouse team for tomorrow's Caulfield Cup is likely to be strengthened with the inclusion of Iron Horse. The four-year-old will be ridden by Greg Hall and joined by three other Waterhouse stayers, Nothin' Leica Dane, Electronic and Hula Flight.Page 44.
THE AGE

Blue-collar club Footscray is set to discard its working class image, as it seeks to ensure it has a long-term future with the Australian Football League. A taskforce has been appointed by the Footscray board to examine, restructure, reform and refashion the club's tough image. Page C10.

Geelong is expected to post an operating profit this year of A$600,000, making it one of the most consistently strong Victorian-based clubs in the Australian Football League. St Kilda posted A$200,000 and Collingwood will make a net loss for the year. The club with the highest profit is Adelaide, posting a massive operating profit of A$1.7 million. Page C9.

Australia's Olympic road cyclist Steven Hodge came in first to the top of Mt Buffalo and by doing so, took out stage nine of the VicHealth Tour. Hodge still remains focused on the prestigious cycle race. Page C9.
HERALD SUN

After riding his first double of the season in Hong Kong on Wednesday, champion Australian jockey Damien Oliver was confident of winning another Caulfield Cup on Doriemus this year, having already won three of the past four Caulfield Cups and the Caulfiel-Melbourne Cup double last year. Page 120.
The football career of 35-year-old veteran Justin Madden is in doubt today as his club Carlton makes final deletions to its playing list before lodging it with the AFL by today's deadline. Page 117.

Former cricket Test spinner Bishen Bedi has offered his advice to two Australian Test novices, Bradley Hogg and Peter McIntyre, in Delhi this week, telling Hogg to slow down at the point of delivery and McIntyre to work on his follow-through.
Page 108.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

When Super League announces plans for its parallel northern and southern hemisphere premierships next week, details of a 22-team - 12 from the Euro League and 10 from Australia - integrated competition will be released. Page 120.

Having already claimed her second successive World Cup title after winning the Auckland race last weekend, 24-year-old triathlete Emma Carney said yesterday that there was no question she is the most dominant and consistent performer on the rich ITU tour.Page 120.

Former Australian Institute of Sport netball head coach Wilma Shakespeare last night attacked both the AIS and Netball Australia, claiming they were misdirecting the sport by failing to establish an elite program for netball that was coordinated nationally. Page 118.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
